checks.note: The rationale and outcome hold up (open_horizon, unresolved), and ARC Prize's caution is backed by e2. But the published e2 excerpt is only "published evidence". It leaves out the finding itself ("does not yet support concluding... AGI"), so it cannot support the relation it is cited for. Also, e2 gives the date as 2026-09-14 while the source page shows 10 September 2026. The 'updated assessment' that would explain the gap is not visible in the evidence.

The proposition, conditions and outcome (causal_assessment, not_applicable, unresolved) match. The e1 excerpt "RNNs fail spectacularly." drops the condition "when generalization requires systematic compositional skills". The abstract also says RNNs succeed when train/test differences are small, so the fragment misstates the finding as a general failure. The e2 fragment "even if that meant facing lawsuits." loses its subject (Meta's discussion of gathering copyrighted data).

overclaims: Synthetic-data experiments also show that effective supply is not fixed.
checks.note: The outcome matches (open_horizon, unresolved). The e3 excerpt "there's little real-world data left" drops "Elon Musk concurs with other AI experts that", so an assertion reads as reported fact. The e1 excerpt "between 2026 and 2032." drops both the 80% confidence interval and what is being projected. The rationale says the synthetic-data study 'shows' supply is not fixed. The study found only conditional benefits: mixtures help, but synthetic data alone was no faster (rephrased) or worse (textbook-style).

The contract lists 'configurations dominant over the last three decades' as an explicit source element and reads 'enough' as enough for reliable generalization by neural networks. Yet the proposition is the bare 'never enough data' and conditions is empty, which leaves out the scope. The e2 excerpt drops "on traditionally hard tasks (such as parity and addition)", which makes a task-specific gain look general. The e3 excerpt "through extended test-time thinking." is a fragment that conveys none of the cited finding.
